opportunity_map.area: Freight counter and station phone (8 stations)
opportunity_map.what_could_change: CSA spec verbatim, 'greeting and assisting customers with shipping, receiving or locating their freight either over-the-counter or on the telephone'. Every 'where is it' answer costs a person at a station. Plain software removes most of the routine share. AI not required for the lookup itself.

opportunity_map.area: Arrival notification and the storage-fee clock
opportunity_map.what_could_change: Tariff says storage fees apply after 'three days after written notification of arrival at the destination point' at '$.75 per 100 pounds or part thereof, per day'. That written notice is a per-shipment obligation AND the legal clock-start for a billable fee. Deterministic workflow automation can generate, deliver and timestamp every notice. No model needed in the customer-facing message.

The tariff is fully published and fully deterministic. Four brackets, $30.00 minimum, 6.25% excise, $30.00 hazmat, Priority at 140%, oversize 140%, human remains 200%, dim weight (LxWxH)/166, same-flight $.35/lb, backhaul 75%. That is arithmetic, not intelligence. Zero AI.

opportunity_map.area: Shipment tracking and the bypass mail gap
opportunity_map.what_could_change: Ryan Air's tracker accepts Booking, Air Waybill, Consolidation or Tracking Numbers. Everts, on the SAME Takeflite platform, also accepts a Bypass Mail Order number. Capability exists on a platform Ryan Air already pays for. Configuration and product work, not AI.
Lynden pushes five milestones by email at instant, hourly or daily frequency across five of Ryan Air's stations. Event-driven notification is table stakes here. Workflow automation, not AI.

opportunity_map.area: Bypass mail processing and daily reconciliation
opportunity_map.what_could_change: Lead Cargo Agent spec, 'Ensures that an on hand reconciliation is completed daily'. That daily reconciliation is an existing, structured, station-level artifact. It can seed arrival notices and an audit-grade movement record with no new integration. Document extraction helps if the count lives on paper.

OIG 22-090-R22 found $346,649 in overpayments and recommends 'a solution that will provide visibility over mail movement in Alaska'. Those recommendations land on USPS, NOT on Ryan Air, so this is direction of travel rather than a current obligation. Software and reporting, not AI.

opportunity_map.area: Dispatch and traffic coordination (village weather and runway conditions)
opportunity_map.what_could_change: Traffic Coordinator obtains and relays village weather and runway conditions continually. VEIA is >90 percent accurate on low visibility from existing FAA camera feeds. Real tech, real relevance. Also safety-critical with a catastrophic cost of error, and the human relay IS the control. We would not build in this lane and we say so.

opportunity_map.area: Load planning across a mixed fleet
opportunity_map.what_could_change: Payloads differ sharply, 1,100 to 7,500 lb, across 7-8 hubs and 70-80 villages. Optimization genuinely fits solvers. No pain about load planning is cited anywhere, so this is a map entry, not an opportunity. Do not build on a wish.

opportunity_map.area: Passenger booking and the 16 hour cutoff
opportunity_map.what_could_change: The short-notice window is exactly the window a bush passenger needs, and it is phone-only. A booking rules engine could open part of it. Any automated agent quoting availability inherits Moffatt liability, so deterministic rules, not a bot.
Two phone calls per refund, one to request and one to chase, both to a specific station, with a 10 business day SLA. A status page and a request form remove the chase call. Plain software.

Deciding whether the weather / mechanical / beyond-control exception applies is judgment with money attached. Gartner puts dynamic cost trade-offs and ethical judgment outside agentic AI before 2027. Software can assemble the evidence pack, a human decides.

Six required fields, no stated response time, acknowledgement, disclaimer or terms, page last modified 2022. An acknowledgement and a routing rule are a form-builder change. Volume unknown, so size unknown.

Everts' own map names 'Aniak - Ryan Air' and 'Nome - Ryan Air' as its ground handler, and the CSA spec includes ground service contracts paperwork. Ryan Air runs a paperwork and billing stream for a company that also competes with it at four overlapping stations. Any customer-facing visibility tool must be partitioned so one carrier's freight never appears in another's view. Hard design constraint.

Traffic Coordinator 'Prepares and completes flight and accounting paperwork for Anchorage Accounting Department', and all eight stations publish a fax number. Paper and rekeying from remote stations to HQ is the classic document-extraction case. Real AI fit, but the evidence is a job spec rather than a stated complaint, so second tier.

Two Technical Records Assistant postings three days apart plus a maintenance tech posting. Heavy document domain with a hard audit trail. Only evidence is job postings, which is not a documented pain. Map entry only.

Ten open roles, four in Bethel, explicitly cross-trained ('Serves as Cargo or Customer Service Agent, as needed'). A new agent must hold a multi-modifier tariff in their head. Internal retrieval over tariff and station procedures is a genuine fit, limited by a corpus with verified holes.

Freight Rules page, read in full, publishes NO freight cutoff, NO claims procedure, NO embargo policy, NO perishables handling. Alaska Air Cargo publishes station hours and cooler/freezer availability. Nothing here is an AI problem. Each missing policy is a phone call that did not need to happen. Highest return per hour on the whole map, and we hand it over free.

Six customer-facing pages unchanged since 2022 or 2024 while nine others changed in the last six weeks. That is a prioritization pattern, NOT neglect. The rates team is resourced, the self-service layer has no owner. Any build we ship needs a named owner or it joins the 2022 shelf.

Ryan Air is one of six Saltchuk Aviation companies. Northern Air Cargo, a sibling, already runs a self-serve rate estimator across sixteen cargo categories. So there is a sibling precedent inside the family, which helps the case and also means a shared-services team may claim the work. Business-viability fact, belongs in the risk gate.

outcome: Move routine freight status and arrival notice work off the station phone and counter, and turn arrival notification into a recorded event instead of a conversation. Two falsifiable measures at one pilot hub over two quarters from go-live. First, the share of arriving freight shipments receiving a timestamped written arrival notice within 24 hours of arrival rises from a two-week measured baseline to 90 percent or better, with the notice and timestamp retained as the storage-clock record their own tariff depends on. Second, station-agent minutes spent on 'where is my freight' and 'has it landed' contacts at that hub fall by a third against a stopwatch baseline taken before go-live. A hard guardrail sits on both: zero increase in customer-facing statements of rate or policy that turn out to be wrong, because under Moffatt v. Air Canada the carrier owns what its systems tell a customer. If agent minutes fall while wrong notices rise, the build failed whatever the first number says.

opportunities_scored.job: When my freight lands in the village, tell me in writing that it is here, so I can collect it before storage fees start
opportunities_scored.note: Satisfaction is 4 not 1 because a named role already does this and it evidently works. What is missing is the written, timestamped, per-shipment record, and that record is the clock-start for a billable fee in their own tariff. The only job where the carrier's own policy creates the obligation, so value lands whether or not a customer changes behavior.

opportunities_scored.job: Get me a current picture of village weather and runway conditions so I can fly safely
opportunities_scored.note: Ties for top and we rule it out deliberately. Cost of error is a human life, the human relay is the safety control, and the tooling that exists is a government research asset pilots already access. Saying no here is the point of running the map.

opportunities_scored.job: Find the hours, freight cutoff, claims procedure, embargo rules and perishables handling without phoning anyone
opportunities_scored.note: Ties for highest and needs no AI, no integration, no vendor. Five policy decisions and a web edit. We tell them free and do not dress it up as a product.

opportunities_scored.job: Tell me where my shipment is right now without me calling a station
opportunities_scored.note: Credit where due, a live tracker exists on Takeflite and accepts four number types. The gap is discoverability and the missing push, not absence of a tracker.

opportunities_scored.job: Tell me what this shipment will cost before I haul it to the counter
opportunities_scored.note: Rates are published and current. The problem is a shipper must run six rules in their head. NAC, which already solved this, is a sibling inside Saltchuk Aviation.

opportunities_scored.job: Track my bypass mail order the way I can with the carrier next door
opportunities_scored.note: Sharpest single competitive fact, verified on both sides on the same platform. Overlaps the status job and should not be double counted. Whether Ryan Air can simply enable it is a Takeflite configuration question we can't verify from outside, so the discount belongs on the solution, not the need.

opportunities_scored.job: Open a freight account and manage my shipping without a fax or a counter visit
opportunities_scored.note: Real verified gap. Also the largest to build, and it touches billing and credit terms, a finance and legal decision at group level.

opportunities_scored.job: Get station paperwork to Anchorage Accounting without anyone rekeying it
opportunities_scored.note: Genuine document-extraction fit, one of the few places a model earns its keep. Evidence is a job description not a stated complaint, and we have no volume, error rate or cycle time. Later lane.

opportunities_scored.job: Answer the tariff and policy question a new agent has not memorized yet
opportunities_scored.note: Textbook retrieval fit, and the corpus is the catch. Four verified holes in the very page it would read, so an honest assistant answers 'not stated' on exactly the questions asked most. Fix the corpus first.

opportunities_scored.job: Close the daily on-hand reconciliation without hunting for freight
opportunities_scored.note: The process exists and holds. The interesting part is not the pain, it is that this artifact is a station-level daily structured list of what is physically on hand at a destination, which is very close to a list of what has arrived and not been collected.

opportunities_scored.job: Decide fairly and quickly whether a mishandled Priority shipment owes a refund
opportunities_scored.note: Assembling evidence for a human is fair game. Deciding is not.

opportunities_scored.job: Prove to USPS what mail moved, when, and at what weight
opportunities_scored.note: Deliberately scored down. The recommendations bind USPS, not Ryan Air, and we have no evidence of a Ryan Air pain here. Not a case we should sell on today.

opportunities_scored.job: Keep aircraft technical records current and audit-ready
opportunities_scored.note: Two postings three days apart is suggestive, not evidence. Regulated domain where an error is an airworthiness problem. Map entry only. We will not build a case on a job board.

opportunities_scored.job: Run the ground handling contract paperwork for another carrier's freight
opportunities_scored.note: The strategically interesting fact is not the paperwork, it is that a competitor at four shared stations is also a handling customer at two. Design constraint, not an opportunity.

opportunities_scored.job: Get an answer to a charter request
opportunities_scored.note: Real line, but no volume, conversion rate or complaint. Low score is honest, not dismissive.

target_opportunity.job: When my freight lands in the village, tell me in writing that it is here, so I can collect it before storage fees start.
target_opportunity.why: Three jobs tied at the top and two get ruled out on their merits. Weather and runway scores 14 and we refuse it, because the cost of error is a life and the human relay is the safety control. Missing policy pages score 14 and need no AI at all, so we hand that over free rather than sell it. That leaves the arrival notice job, strongest of the three on Torres's four factors anyway. Sizing, it touches every arriving freight shipment across up to eight hubs feeding 70 to 80 villages, in what their own about page calls their primary business. Market position, Lynden already pushes five milestone emails across five of the same stations and Everts already exposes bypass mail order tracking on the very same Takeflite platform, so the shipper's expectation is already set by the carrier next door. Strategy fit, this is the one job where the carrier's own published tariff creates the obligation rather than a customer creating a request, since storage fees only start three days after written notification of arrival, which makes the notice simultaneously a service, a cost reduction and the evidentiary basis for a fee they already publish. Care versus satisfaction, a named full-time role currently spends its day relaying ETAs and load onboard by phone while four of ten open positions sit at Bethel, so the manual path is being staffed at the moment it is hardest to staff.
target_opportunity.four_forces: Push, their own tariff makes a written arrival notice the clock-start for a billable storage fee, so an un-notified shipment is a customer in the dark and a fee that is hard to defend, and the Traffic Coordinator role spends its day on that relay while ten roles sit open. Pull, Lynden already delivers five milestone emails across Bethel, Emmonak, Kotzebue, Nome and St. Mary's, and Everts already exposes bypass mail order tracking on the same platform, so this matches what shippers can already get rather than inventing a category. Anxiety is the strong force and deserves respect. Moffatt v. Air Canada held that a carrier is responsible for all the information on its website, so a wrong automated notice is theirs to own, and a wrong arrival notice is worse than silence because it starts a fee clock incorrectly and becomes a billing dispute. Gnosis Freight's warning applies directly, AI amplifies whatever you feed it, and the notice is only as good as the underlying scan. Habit, the phone, the counter and the village agent are the trusted channel and they work, all eight stations still publish a fax, and Takeflite is deeply embedded with Grant Aviation reporting 90 percent of operational employees interacting with it daily, so anything asking an agent to work outside their existing screen loses to habit. VERDICT, push plus pull clears anxiety plus habit ONLY if the build is deterministic in the customer path, triggered by an event a human already confirms, reversible by a station agent before it sends, and silent about rates and policy in free text. Anxiety is retired by design choices, not by reassurance. If the build has to promise it will be careful, it is the wrong build.

candidates.name: Arrival Notice Desk, driven by the daily on-hand reconciliation
candidates.build_type: Workflow automation with a narrow document-extraction model, human in the loop
candidates.what_it_does: Rides a process the station is already required to run. The Lead Cargo Agent spec says an on-hand reconciliation is completed daily, so each station already produces a daily list of what is physically sitting at a destination. The desk ingests that list, diffs it against yesterday to identify what newly arrived, and drafts a written arrival notice per consignee with the shipment reference, the arrival timestamp and the date storage fees would begin under the published rule. A station agent reviews the batch on one screen and releases it, or holds any line. Sent notices are stored with their timestamp as the record the tariff's storage clause depends on, and a day-two reminder goes out on anything still uncollected. The only model does document extraction on the reconciliation when it is not already machine readable, and a human confirms its output before anything reaches a customer. The customer-facing message is fully templated, so no model ever writes a sentence a shipper reads.
candidates.cost_of_delay: High and rising. The PRC passed a 9.39 percent Alaska Bypass increase, Ravn cancelled all Alaska flights in August 2025, and coverage names Bering Air and Ryan Air as the only airlines regularly serving the region's villages. Volume and scrutiny concentrate on fewer carriers, so every month of a phone-based notification chain costs more agent minutes than the month before, at a company with ten roles open and four at Bethel. Delay is also paid in storage revenue that is awkward to defend without a written notice on file.

candidates.name: Takeflite Event Notification Engine
candidates.build_type: Workflow automation on a direct platform integration
candidates.what_it_does: The cleaner version of the same idea. Subscribes directly to shipment events in Takeflite and fires templated milestone messages the way Lynden does, with arrival as the anchoring event and the storage clock computed from it. No station step at all, which is both its advantage and its risk.
candidates.cost_of_delay: Low as a standalone. This is the graduation path for the desk rather than a competing destination.
candidates.penalty_reason: Nothing in claims.json establishes that Ryan Air has API access to Takeflite, what its contract permits, or who at Saltchuk Aviation Shared Services would sign it off. Takeflite is a third-party vendor shared with Grant Aviation and Yute, so the integration is theirs to grant. RAND names weak infrastructure and lacking the data among the five root causes of AI project failure, and betting a first engagement on an unverified third-party integration is exactly that bet.

candidates.name: Self-Serve Tracking Upgrade with bypass mail order lookup
candidates.build_type: Plain software, customer-facing product surface, no AI
candidates.what_it_does: Closes the sharpest verified competitive gap. Replaces the bare Track Airbill hyperlink, unchanged since 2022, with a real tracking page carrying instructions and accepting a Bypass Mail Order number the way Everts does on the same platform, plus a subscribe control. Pull rather than push.
candidates.cost_of_delay: Moderate. Everts publishes bypass mail order tracking today at four stations where the two carriers overlap.

candidates.name: Station Voice and Chat Agent for freight status
candidates.what_it_does: The obvious build, included so it can be beaten on the record rather than quietly skipped. Answers the inbound where-is-my-freight call, handles the under-16-hour booking inquiry and refund status chase, escalates the rest.
candidates.cost_of_delay: NEGATIVE. Waiting improves this one. Gartner puts judgment-heavy agentic work outside the window before 2027, and every month of clean event data makes a future voice layer safer rather than less valuable.
candidates.penalty_reason: Moffatt v. Air Canada is directly on point, a carrier owns what its bot tells a customer, and here the bot would be quoting arrival status that starts a fee clock and rate rules with six interacting modifiers. Gartner warns agent washing increases misaligned investment and vendor lock-in. Gnosis Freight describes the failure mode precisely. It also needs the same unverified Takeflite lookup, so it carries candidate two's risk on top of its own.

candidates.name: Tariff Quote Engine
candidates.build_type: Plain software, deterministic rules, no AI whatsoever
candidates.what_it_does: Turns the published tariff into a calculator. Weight bracket, dimensional weight, the $30.00 minimum, 6.25 percent excise, the $30.00 hazmat surcharge, Priority and oversize at 140 percent, human remains at 200 percent, backhaul at 75 percent, same-flight at $.35 per pound. Produces a shareable estimate with the same kind of honest disclaimer NAC already publishes.
candidates.cost_of_delay: Moderate. NAC, Everts and Alaska Air Cargo all publish estimating tools today. Strongest Next-lane item and the natural second phase, because it shares the customer surface phase one creates.
candidates.note: Highest confidence on the board because the full rule set is published verbatim, it is arithmetic with no model and no third-party dependency, and three competitors prove shippers want it, one of which is a Saltchuk sibling.

candidates.name: Internal Station Agent Copilot
candidates.build_type: Retrieval assistant over their own tariff and station procedures, internal only
candidates.what_it_does: Answers the tariff and policy question a cross-trained agent has not memorized, for staff only and never for customers. Internal by design, which keeps it clear of the Moffatt problem.
candidates.cost_of_delay: Low, and sequencing matters more than timing. Publish the missing policies first and this roughly doubles in value. Build it first and it inherits the holes.
candidates.penalty_reason: The corpus is the problem. The freight rules page publishes no freight cutoff, no claims procedure, no embargo policy and no perishables handling, so an honest assistant returns 'not stated' on a large share of what agents actually field. Retrieval can't retrieve what was never written.

candidates.name: Publish the missing policy pages
candidates.build_type: NONE. Not an AI build and not something we would sell.
candidates.what_it_does: Writes down what is already true. A freight cutoff time, a claims procedure, an embargo policy, perishables handling, and station hours per location, the way Alaska Air Cargo publishes hours and cooler or freezer availability. Five decisions and a web edit on a site whose rates and schedule pages were updated within the last six weeks, so the capability plainly exists in-house.
candidates.cost_of_delay: Highest on the board per hour of effort. Every day without these is another day of calls that did not need to be made, at eight stations, while four cargo and customer service roles sit open at Bethel.
candidates.note: THEIR half week, not ours. We recommend it whether or not they ever speak to us, and it goes IN FRONT of the paid work rather than behind it.

provisional_pick.name: Arrival Notice Desk, driven by the daily on-hand reconciliation
provisional_pick.why_over_others: The uncomfortable part first, because it is the whole reason to trust the rest. The highest RICE score on this board by a wide margin is 'Publish the missing policy pages' at 16.2, and it is not an AI build, not a project, and we would not charge for it. Among things we would actually build, the Arrival Notice Desk wins at 2.08. Against the Takeflite Event Notification Engine at 0.66, the event engine is the better PRODUCT and rests entirely on a third-party integration nothing in the record establishes they have, so the desk gets a hub live on a data source we know exists because their own job posting says it is completed daily, and the event engine becomes phase two once access is confirmed. Against the Self-Serve Tracking Upgrade at 0.88, that build is pull and this job is push, and a shipper in a village who does not know the freight landed will not go looking for it. Against the Tariff Quote Engine at 0.85, this is the closest call and the honest one, it carries the highest confidence on the board and loses only because it serves the second-ranked job rather than the target. Against the Internal Copilot at 0.25, retrieval can't retrieve what was never written. Against the Station Voice and Chat Agent at 0.13, this is the build a lazy vendor would lead with and it is last for reasons written in the file, and waiting genuinely improves it, which is the definition of something that should not be phase one. Two facts for the risk gate rather than the score. Ryan Air is one of six Saltchuk Aviation companies, so the buying decision may not sit entirely in Anchorage and Saltchuk Aviation Shared Services could claim this work, which cuts both ways because sibling Northern Air Cargo already runs a self-serve estimator. Second, Everts is named on its own map as a Ryan Air ground handling customer at Aniak and Nome while competing at four shared stations, so any customer-visible surface must be partitioned so one carrier's freight never appears in another's view, from day one. Finally, the shape of the pick answers the anxiety force rather than arguing with it. Deterministic templates in the customer path, a trigger a human already performs daily, an agent who can hold any line before it sends, no model sentence ever reaching a shipper, and no rate or policy stated in free text. Google's first rule of ML applies cleanly, do not be afraid to launch without it, and Anthropic's guidance points the same way. The one model in this system extracts text from a document a human then confirms, which is the least ambitious use of AI on this entire board and the only one that survives the evidence.
